title: SurvTD: Continuous-Time Semi-Markov Temporal Difference Learning for Informative Dynamic Survival Analysis
core_mechanism: Reformulate continuous-time dynamic survival analysis on irregular trajectories as policy evaluation in an absorbing Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP). Between irregular observations t_j and t_{j+1} separated by interval duration \Delta t_j, the model updates future failure distributions via a contractive Survival Bellman Operator that scales multi-bucket survival evidence across \Delta t_j and geometrically unifies n-step returns with a parameter lambda.
core_mechanism_steps: Step 1: Encode irregular longitudinal observations H_{t_j} into latent state representation h_j via a recurrent sequential backbone.
Step 2: Predict discrete conditional hazards h_j(s) over K future discrete buckets, producing survival curve S_j(s) and probability mass function p_j(s).
Step 3: Compute continuous interval duration \Delta t_j = t_{j+1} - t_j and evaluate multi-bucket interval survival probability S_j(\Delta t_j) as state-dependent discount factor.

Step 4: Shift future target probability distribution leftward by \Delta t_j steps and construct Survival Bellman target T p_j(s) = I[Event in \Delta t_j] + S_j(\Delta t_j) * TargetNet(p_{j+1}(s - \Delta t_j)).

Step 5: Synthesize geometric lambda-return G^lambda_j(s) via backward trajectory recursion to smoothly interpolate between 1-step Bellman bootstrapping (lambda=0) and terminal empirical returns (lambda=1).
Step 6: Minimize Cramér distance loss between predicted cumulative distribution F_pred and target cumulative distribution F_{G^lambda} to ensure contractive fixed-point convergence.

gap_closure.gap: Exogenous stationary unit-step assumption in prior survival consistency models (TCSR, DeepTCSR) fails in clinical settings where observation timing is an informative process reflecting patient risk.
gap_closure.how_closed: Pivots from assuming exogenous uniform unit transitions to an endogenous informative continuous observation process, scaling cumulative non-event survival evidence proportionally across elapsed duration \Delta t_j rather than collapsing to a 1-bit unit transition.

gap_closure.gap: Numerical division divergence (div S) and catastrophic gradient variance of terminal Monte Carlo NLL under irregular time horizons.
gap_closure.how_closed: Reframes irregular dynamic survival prediction into policy evaluation over an absorbing Semi-Markov Decision Process, replacing division explosion with contractive multiplication and proving fixed-point convergence under the Cramér Wasserstein-1 metric.

composition_note: Composing assumption_audit_and_pivot with reframe_as_solvable_object is necessary because relaxing the exogenous interval assumption generates continuous, variable-length transition intervals that can only be stably resolved by importing contractive SMDP Bellman policy evaluation machinery.
falsification_prediction: When temporal discount interval duration \Delta t_j is scrambled or uncoupled from elapsed time, discrimination performance drops significantly below baseline C-index (measured in Bleistein2024 as 0.8791 on NASA turbofan degradation) and calibration error increases.
negative_control: Randomize interval_duration_scaling_factor by shuffling observation intervals \Delta t_j across independent patient trajectories, which disables temporal contraction and causes time-dependent AUC and C-index to degrade to baseline performance.
compute_budget: 1x Apple M-series GPU or 1x NVIDIA RTX 3090, training time 20 minutes for 20 epochs on C-MAPSS and simulated ODE benchmarks.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: TCSR requires discrete uniform steps (Delta=1) and divides by survival probability causing divergence; SurvTD operates over continuous irregular intervals (Delta t) with contractive multiplication and multi-step lambda-returns.

CoxSig relies on linear signature regression under proportional hazards and terminal Monte Carlo NLL; SurvTD introduces recursive Survival Bellman temporal difference learning to capture non-linear degradation and mitigate variance.

Dynamic-DeepHit uses terminal Monte Carlo NLL with an ad-hoc pairwise ranking penalty, lacking inter-step Bellman consistency across adjacent observations; SurvTD enforces structural temporal consistency directly via contractive operators.

Alaa et al. model informative clinical observation using point processes (Hawkes jump processes); SurvTD leverages informative intervals directly as continuous-time discount factors in a deep temporal difference learning framework.
